# Question `generator-shortcuts`

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Strongest rival

**Fill every visibly complete blue frame independently from the seed inside that
frame, preserving all blue borders.**

This rival fits all three canonical demonstrations because every demonstrated
frame is disconnected and has one seed.  It is also exactly the behavior the
old generator taught.  The executable authority is broader: it operates on each
4-connected blue object, uses that object's combined bounding box, chooses the
last non-{0,1} interior seed in row-major order, and fills the whole interior.

## Exact disagreement input

The canonical query itself is a discriminator:

```text
00000000000000
01111110000000
01000010011110
01002010010010
01000010010010
01111110017010
00000000010010
00001111111110
00001030100000
00001000100000
00001111100000
```

The right and lower frames touch, so they are one blue component.  The last
seed in that combined bounding box is color 3.  The intended output is:

```text
00000000000000
01111110000000
01222210011110
01222333333310
01222333333310
01111333333310
00000333333310
00001333333310
00001333333300
00001333333300
00001111100000
```

The independent-frame rival instead returns:

```text
00000000000000
01111110000000
01222210011110
01222210017710
01222210017710
01111110017710
00000000017710
00001111111110
00001333100000
00001333100000
00001111100000
```

The outputs differ at 43 cells.  The rival preserves the internal blue borders
and separately fills the upper-right frame with 7 and the lower frame with 3;
the authority overwrites the merged bounding-box interior with 3.

## How I checked it

1. I executed the selected canonical Racket authority through the repository's
   source-bound battery.  `authority_sync` reports exact synchronization across
   canonical, archival, and selected copies and execution parity on 3/3 train
   and 1/1 test pairs.
2. I independently transcribed the rule as `rule_mirror` and checked exact
   equality on every canonical pair.
3. The Racket smoke gate compared the mirror against the authority on 120
   generated inputs: 120/120 equal, 0 crashes.
4. I implemented the rival explicitly as
   `SEMANTIC_RIVALS["fill_each_frame_independently"]`; focused tests and the
   semantic gate verify its disagreement on touching profiles.

## Does the revised generator emit such cases?

**Yes, deliberately and frequently.**  Three of six profiles contain touching
frames, and the cyclic order alternates disconnected and touching scenes.  Every
three-demonstration lesson therefore includes at least one disagreement case.
The semantic gate observed the independent-frame witness on 305/600 sampled
inputs and verified 60/60 direct rival claims.

A compact generated replay is
`seed=30000, sample_index=0, scene_profile="touching_pair_8x12"`:

```text
000000000000
011111000000
015001111110
010001100010
010001100010
011111180010
000000111110
000000000000
```

Authority output:

```text
000000000000
011111000000
018888888810
018888888810
018888888810
018888888810
000000111110
000000000000
```

Independent-frame rival:

```text
000000000000
011111000000
015551111110
015551188810
015551188810
011111188810
000000111110
000000000000
```
